name: ct202-spendlog-disk-retention
note: DISPOSITIONED 2026-09-16 08:40 PT, SCHEDULED TICK #282 - Do NOT requeue. SUPERSEDED by task 170 (active entry 9999j-170-spendlog-retention-not-live.json). Evidence read this tick: the LEDGER already records the supersede ('task 115's spendlog retention is superseded by task 170'), and 170's own note carries the measurement that closed 115's claim - live prod router GET /config/list?config_type=general_settings shows maximum_spend_logs_retention_period=None and store_prompts_in_spend_logs=True, i.e. 115 was closed on a claim the live router contradicts. Run 20260910T085335Z_c02e3a06 reads failed; that failure is real but irrelevant - the WORK now belongs to 170, so requeuing 115 would duplicate an active task. || PRIOR NOTE: PAXTON DECISION 2026-09-09: 7-DAY retention window. But 7 days of FULL payloads = 35-77G which does NOT fit the 80G disk (86-138%). So the 7-day window requires EITHER (A default, recommended) store_prompts_in_spend_logs:false so retention costs ~0.5G and is trivially sustainable while keeping accounting, OR (B) move the postgres-data volume to a bigger mount (Paxton /point option, host change), OR (C) grow CT202 disk (Paxton has standing disk-growth authorisation). Default to A unless bodies are needed for audit. Data IS in Postgres (docker volume on ZFS), so movable. URGENT (1-3 days to 80% on the PROD router box) but not an emergency. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND VERIFIED: CT202 disk growth is Postgres LiteLLM_SpendLogs TOAST - the full prompt/response JSON of every gateway request, 18G, no retention policy in EITHER the yaml OR the DB LiteLLM_Config row. Verified by the overseer independently: postgres-data volume du = 18G (dominant), disk 65% and climbing. Daily payload doubling since Sep 05 (450MB -> 6907MB on Sep 09); 90% of the 18G written in 7 days. This is the box that silently hit 100% on 2026-09-08 and killed the prod router for ~1h, destroying 23 runs, with nothing on any operator surface showing it. Two drivers, both with ZERO active runs: overseer-ingest chatter (7200 rows/hr, mostly repeated MCP:list_tools) and long-context lh-harness routes (nemotron 3MB/row, kimi-k2.6 9.7MB/row). FIX ORDER: (1) store_prompts_in_spend_logs:false kills 95% of the FLOW - heap is only 490M so accounting survives; (2) maximum_spend_logs_retention_period ~3-7 days; (3) pg_repack to reclaim the 18G - a plain DELETE frees nothing, VACUUM FULL locks the prod DB so needs a WINDOW; (4) docker builder prune frees 10-16G at 0 active - lowest risk, needs Paxton's go on a prod-box mutation; (8) a disk ALARM at 75% - both fills were silent, this is the highest-leverage prevention. HAZARDS baked in: LiteLLM_Config DB row wins over yaml (POST /config/update then read back and diff); any litellm-config.yaml edit force-recreates the prod router (zero active runs, no gate mid-flight); ZFS snapshot destroy is a host change on ptait01 needing explicit go+rollback+window; never the bare gateway /health. READ-ONLY until a window - nothing on CT202 mutated until approved. Do NOT push or open a PR - commit and state which steps need Paxton's window/go.
